newsitem.title: UK: Police study N.Ireland march request.
newsitem.headline: Police study N.Ireland march request.

text.p: Northern Ireland police said on Friday they had yet to decide whether to grant permission for a controversial Protestant march on Saturday which has aroused fears of inflaming sectarian tensions.

Police in Northern Ireland's second city, Londonderry, said a decision on whether to allow the march on Saturday to go ahead would be taken in the light of contacts between Protestant and Roman Catholic representatives.
Saturday's planned march by the Apprentice Boys has been opposed by Catholic Irish nationalists in the city who say it is an unnneeded confrontation during a tense period in the province.
Residents of the Catholic Bogside area of the city plan to hold a counter parade along the walls of Londonderry at exactly the same time as some 200 members of the Apprentice order.
They have also called on their supporters to stage a peaceful rally beneath the walls to show their condemnation of the parade.
Police said a decision on whether to let the Apprentice Boys march would be taken later on Friday or possibly early on Saturday depending upon negotiations between representatives of the two sides.
The original march was rerouted on August 10 when sectarian violence flared across Northern Ireland during the annual marching season by members of the 60-percent Protestant majority.
Martin McGuinness, a senior member of the IRA's Sinn Fein political wing, has accused the Apprentice Boys of seeking confrontation by going ahead with the march.
